decision.chip_justification: The solver's chip calendar puts the first-set Bench Boost in this gameweek. The EV panel says it adds +14.7 points in GW8, against a bar of 9.1 for playing it now. Its best week otherwise would be GW16 at +11.7, so we gain about 3 points by playing it now instead of waiting. The path also wants the Triple Captain in GW9, so the boost cannot go there without pushing the TC back. All four bench players are projected to play real minutes: Verbruggen 90, Muharemović 90, Lewis-Potter 74, João Pedro 68. My searches found no current injury for any of them. João Pedro is the one risk. He had a knee problem in early October and I could not find a fresh update, but the projection treats him as fit, and the market is buying him back in, which fits with him being available. Even with him blanking, the boost should still clear the bar. What we give up is the chance to use it in GW16 or to build a better bench for it later. That is worth less than this week's number, and last week's review told us to play a chip when it clears its bar and the only doubt is vague.
decision.rationale:
WHAT I DID
One transfer: Vuskovic out, Konsa (Arsenal, £4.6m) in, no hit. I played the Bench Boost. Captain is Mbeumo, vice-captain Saka. I picked Mbeumo over Haaland because Haaland is a fitness doubt this week.

WHAT I LEARNED
- Konsa (the player we're buying): he had a thigh/quad scare on England duty in early October. That has cleared. He started at the City Ground last weekend, and every preview of Wednesday's Bayern game has him at centre-back next to Gabriel. Saliba is out with a back injury, so Konsa is first choice. Arsenal list no doubts. I set him to 88 minutes (the model had 90).
- Calafiori and Saka are both expected to start in Munich. One small worry for Calafiori: Hincapié is due back for the Everton game and could compete for left-back.
- Guéhi: this was a re-check. He took City's press conference on 19 Oct and called himself fit and healthy. City are playing four games in ten days, so I kept him at 80 minutes for rotation (model had 90).
- Haaland: he took a foot knock late against Ipswich. Maresca said he could be available, but he needed assessing and previews expected him to be rested on Tuesday. I left him at 65 minutes as a doubt (model had 88). That is why he isn't captain.
- Saved from earlier runs, not searched again: Tavernier set to 85 minutes (model had 79), Thomas to 88 (model had 90).
- Bench: no current injury news for Verbruggen, Muharemović or Lewis-Potter. João Pedro had a knee problem in early October and I found no update since. The model has him fit at 68 minutes, which is the one real risk to the boost. I ran out of searches before Brighton, Leeds, Brentford, Chelsea or Man Utd had held their GW8 press conferences, so any late news from Friday is not in this.

WHY THIS PLAN
After my changes, the solver still picks this plan, and it beats rolling the transfer by about 0.8 net points. That's a small margin. I'm making the move because I checked Konsa is fit and starting, because Vuskovic was the weakest projection in the squad, and because the solver's path wants Konsa eventually anyway (the roll plan buys him next week). We still bank free transfers for next week's moves (Tarkowski in the path). I turned down the hit plans (6 and 7): taking a 4-point hit doesn't pay for itself on these numbers. The Bench Boost is worth +14.7 against a bar of 9.1, and its best later week is only +11.7 in GW16. I captained Mbeumo because he is projected around 5.4 and certain to play, while Haaland's projection drops with the doubt over his foot. Price note: Groß, Tavernier and Calafiori are rising, but none of that affected this plan.
